theorem_title: No-return of the wall trace implies the Nice Angel theorem
formal_statement: theorem AngelDevil.niceAngelWins_of_wall_no_return (hreturn : ∀ D, AngelDevil.Nice 2 D → ∀ n, 0 < n → AngelDevil.wallTrace D n ≠ AngelDevil.initialWall) : AngelDevil.NiceAngelWins 2 := by sorry
natural_language_statement: Assume that against every Nice Devil, the specified two-transition wall trace never returns to its initial directed wall at a positive index. Then there is one power-two Angel strategy that survives against every Nice Devil and, against each such Devil, leaves every finite box centered at the origin. The no-return premise is an explicit geometric assumption; this conditional theorem does not by itself establish that premise.
source: Mathe, The Angel of power 2 wins (2007), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548306008303; author manuscript pp. 6-8, octagonal wall-following rule, Claim 3.1 analogue, Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.5. Two wall transitions per turn give an admissible power-two implementation; no-return is the remaining geometric obligation.
